title: Mommy Got Lost
vol: Mommy Is Human Too · Book Twelve
verse: "In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths."

pages.text:
They piled into the car to visit Auntie's brand-new place,
with snacks and songs and Baby Bee with crackers on her face.

Mommy drove and drove and drove, past bridges, shops, and trees.
"I know the way," she told them all. "I'll get us there with ease."

But then the roads looked different, and the signs looked strange and new,
and Mommy's hands grew tighter on the wheel — she had no clue.

"Are we there yet?" Jojo asked. "Are we there yet?" Pip asked, too.
And Mommy said, "Not yet," and then, "Not yet," and "Not yet" — it's true.

They passed the same red gas station once, and twice, and then once more.
"Hey, Mommy," Jojo said, "I think we passed that store before!"

And Mommy pulled the car aside and let out a long sigh:
"I'm lost," she said. "I thought I knew. I really did. Oh my."

The car got very quiet. Pip's eyes went big and wide.
"But Mommies always know the way," she whispered from her side.

"Not always, Pip," said Mommy. "Grown-ups take wrong turns, it's true.
And when we do, the brave thing is to ask for help. That's what we do."

So Mommy called up Auntie, and she listened, word by word:
"Turn left at the big white church, then right" — the clearest thing she'd heard.

And Jojo watched for the big white church, and Pip watched for the sign,
and Baby Bee watched Biscuit's tail — and everything was fine.

"Thank you, team," said Mommy. "I could not have done it alone.
Asking isn't failing. That's how grown-ups find their way home."

They pulled up late to Auntie's with a honk and with a cheer,
and Auntie laughed, "You made it! Come on in — you're finally here!"

And Jojo said, "When I get lost, I'll ask for help, like you."
And Mommy smiled. "And so will I. I'm always learning too."

Because your Mommy drives and plans and leads the whole day through —
and Mommy takes wrong turns sometimes… because she's human too.

verses: I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye.
Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it.
Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
